quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
A bicycle repair shop is ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be on the road ahead.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow, what should you do?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Come to a complete stop.
You can turn left if you yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can turn left if you yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians crossing the street.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and keep going.
Stop right away.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless it is unsafe to stop.
Speed up to get through before the light turns red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless it is unsafe to stop.
questions.explanation: When the light turns yellow, slow down and stop before you enter the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, you may carefully drive through.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. Slow down as you approach the intersection and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if necessary.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with no stop sign or traffic light?

options.text: Keep your speed and continue.
Stop, look both ways, then proceed.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to any vehicle coming from your right. Always be ready to yield by slowing down and watching carefully in all directions.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) is affected by all of these except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
The time between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your body weight. Being physically fit does not change your BAC.

questions.question: How long do you have to tell the Department of Licensing about your new address?

options.text: Within 10 days.
Within 30 days.
At your next license renewal.
When your license no longer matches your checkbook.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 10 days.
questions.explanation: You must notify the Department of Licensing within 10 days if you change your address or legal name.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set your parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires pointing straight.
Turn the steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn the steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill, turn the steering wheel away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: How long must your turn signal be on before you change direction?

options.text: 50 feet.
75 feet.
100 feet.
125 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet.
questions.explanation: Signal for at least 100 feet before you change direction.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Other drivers can follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with one rider.
You must move completely into the other lane to pass a motorcycle.
A motorcycle's brake lights turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the other lane to pass a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane of space. Be sure your entire vehicle is in the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Use too much oil.
Require your vehicle to need a tune-up sooner.
Make you feel tired while driving.
Start fires on grass near roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you feel tired while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases from the engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust system can be dangerous and make you feel drowsy while driving.

questions.question: What is a "No zone?"

options.text: A no passing zone
A one-way traffic area
A blind spot around a large vehicle
An area for motor vehicles only

questions.correctAnswerText: A blind spot around a large vehicle
questions.explanation: A "No zone" is a large blind spot around trucks and other large vehicles. Stay away from these areas.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb:

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill, turn your wheels away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels straight.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the side of the road. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic lanes moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: If you see this sign, you:

options.text: Cannot pass another vehicle.
May pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
May pass if you know the road ahead.
May pass only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white and rectangular with black markings. Drivers must obey them. This sign means passing is not allowed.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow an instruction are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: Round signs indicate:

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers that a railroad crossing is coming. Be extra careful at railroad crossings.

questions.question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving the same direction. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by traffic. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Wait until you can pass through the intersection completely.
Use your horn to move traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can pass through the intersection completely.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot get completely across it. Wait for traffic to clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: It is illegal for drivers under 21 to drive with a THC level above ____ per milliliter of blood.

options.text: Zero nanograms
One nanogram
Three nanograms
Five nanograms

questions.correctAnswerText: Zero nanograms
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot drive with any detectable THC in their blood. Drivers 21 and older can have up to five nanograms per milliliter. Driving under the influence of marijuana is dangerous.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road slants toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will be required to turn left just ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the side of the road marks the edge between the driving lane and the shoulder. If the line angles toward the middle of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. Hot weather makes this worse by bringing up even more oil.

questions.question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when you stop on:

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on roads with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do before moving your car?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing up. Look through your back window and do not rely only on mirrors. Children can be hidden from your view, so a physical check is essential.
